chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When it is the last night of the month of Ramadan, say: 'O Allah, this is the month of Ramadan in which You revealed the Quran, and it is coming to an end, and I seek refuge with Your noble Face, O Lord, lest the dawn rise from this night of mine, or the month of Ramadan pass away, while there is a debt or sin against me for which You intend to punish me on the Day I meet You.'

key_terms.تَصَرَّمَ: Passed away / came to an end

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for the last night of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the concept of 'Tabi'ah' (accountability or debt) owed to Allah, reflecting the Shia scholarly focus on meticulous self-examination before the month's conclusion. It serves as a spiritual preparation for Laylat al-Qadr, urging the believer to seek refuge from any unatoned sins that might result in divine punishment upon meeting Allah.
